newsitem.title: GERMANY: German sports channel wins supreme court battle.
newsitem.headline: German sports channel wins supreme court battle.

text.p: Germany's Constitutional Court on Thursday overturned a regulatory ruling that had sought to block a sports channel owned by Munich media mogul Leo Kirch from broadcasting outside Bavaria.

The decision was good news for Kirch, who suffered a setback this week in another court case involving his digital pay TV activities, as it puts to rest suits brought against the company by media regulators in Berlin and Brandenburg states.

The Berlin/Brandenburg media authority had appealed to the Constitutional Court after both the Bavarian media regulators and the Bavarian Constitutional Court rejected its suit to rescind the licence for Kirch's DSF sports channel.

"Of course we are very happy about this decision, which we think is correct," DSF said in a statement. "After all we have to concentrate our real purpose, which is competent reporting of sports events."
Media regulators in Berlin and Brandenburg states objected to approving the broadcaster's licence in 1993 because they believe Kirch already holds too much broadcasting power.
Kirch owns 50 percent of DSF and controls Germany's second-largest commercial broadcaster SAT1.
But DSF is not completely out of the woods yet. Another suit against it is still under consideration by Germany's Adminstrative Court.
